- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Make selective `core_attn` recomputation release the attention output retained by the output projection, reducing activation memory with fused attention.

In our fused-attention comparison, enabling ordinary `core_attn` checkpointing did not reduce peak activation memory. The output projection still saves the core-attention output for its weight gradient. This PR replaces ordinary checkpointing with `CheckpointWithoutOutput`: discard the attention output after projection and restore it before projection backward consumes it. The existing selective-recompute configuration remains the entry point.

Register recomputation on the projection output so that restoration precedes both projection backward and optional output-gate backward. When `mla_up_proj` recomputation is also enabled, register its hook first on the same tensor: restore Q/K/V, then recompute core attention.

Reject selective `core_attn` recomputation combined with `attn_proj` activation offloading during configuration validation, because both manage the projection-input storage. Remove the obsolete fused-attention recomputation warning and update the existing documentation to classify `core_attn` as output-discarding checkpointing.

## Issue tracking

Related to [#1886](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/1886), which reports no memory reduction with `core_attn` checkpointing and uses fused attention in its reproducer. This change improves memory savings by releasing the attention output retained for projection backward.

## Validation

### Added unit tests

- `tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_core_attention_recompute.py`: 32 parameterized GPU / Transformer Engine cases (4 attention variants × 2 sequence layouts × 2 dropout settings × 2 backends). Cover MHA, gated attention, MLA, and MLA with up-projection recomputation; packed/unpacked inputs; and FlashAttention/fused attention. Check storage discard/restoration, outputs, input/parameter gradients, and two outstanding forward graphs.
- `tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_transformer_config.py`: 24 added parameterized cases, comprising 12 conflict-rejection cases and 12 nonconflicting cases across `TransformerConfig` and `MLATransformerConfig`.

### End-to-end training

Separately from the committed unit tests, we ran five end-to-end DeepSeek-V2 Lite training controls.

Configuration: one node with 8 devices; 27 layers, hidden size 2048, 16 attention heads, sequence length 4096, BF16, FlashAttention, TP=1 / PP=4 / EP=2 / DP=2, microbatch size 1, global batch size 8, mock data, seed 42, and 20 training steps. All controls use the same execution environment and fusion settings. Initial parameter hashes match at every rank.

All five runs complete 20 forward/backward and optimizer steps, exit successfully, and record finite losses and gradient norms with no skipped steps.

#### Activation memory

Report the maximum of the per-rank `max_memory_allocated` measurements for training step 20.

| Recompute configuration | Step-20 max allocated memory (GiB) | Step-20 training loss |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Ordinary `core_attn` checkpoint | 54.107 | 8.733608 |
| Ordinary `core_attn`, independent repeat | 54.091 | 8.737156 |
| Discard-output `core_attn` | 53.663 | 8.736550 |
| Ordinary `core_attn` + `mla_up_proj` | 51.782 | 8.745314 |
| Discard-output `core_attn` + `mla_up_proj` | 51.338 | 8.740759 |

Switching core attention to discard-output reduces peak allocated memory by **0.444 GiB (454.6 MiB)**. With `mla_up_proj` recomputation already enabled, it saves a further **0.444 GiB (454.9 MiB)** relative to the matching ordinary-core-checkpoint control. Instrumentation also confirms that the core-attention output storage is released after projection.

#### Training numerical consistency

Compare matching iterations across all 20 steps. Gradient-norm differences below refer to the scalar norm logged by the trainer.

| Comparison | Maximum absolute loss difference | Maximum relative gradient-norm difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Independent repeat vs. ordinary `core_attn` baseline | 0.014456 | 1.937% |
| Discard-output vs. ordinary `core_attn` | 0.003868 | 0.584% |
| Discard-output vs. ordinary `core_attn`, both with `mla_up_proj` | 0.007325 | 1.118% |

For `core_attn` alone, both differences are smaller than those observed between independent baseline repeats. These measurements assess short-run training consistency over 20 steps with mock data.

- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [x] I have added proper typing to my new production method
- [x] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the full autoformatter script on my PR

**Restore input-layernorm output before MLA up-projection replay.**

**Failure:** Build a training `TransformerLayer` with the TE MLA submodules, `q_lora_rank=None`, and selective `recompute_modules=["layernorm", "mla_up_proj"]`; run forward and backward on a gradient-enabled input. Without Q-LoRA, [`_qkv_down_projection`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/091d511c133395734cbffe805191959cfbd6430a/megatron/core/transformer/multi_latent_attention.py#L727-L746) passes the normalized hidden states directly through as `q_compressed`. That tensor becomes a saved input of the up-projection checkpoint.

This change registers up-projection replay on the projection output **before** the enclosing layer registers its [input-layernorm restoration hook](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/091d511c133395734cbffe805191959cfbd6430a/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L743-L749) on the same tensor. Hooks execute in registration order, so up-projection replay reads the still-discarded, zero-byte normalized input. Backward must instead restore that input before recomputing `linear_q_proj`. The [base implementation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b67127774ca558442fb566a3df6a50862c04e4b8/megatron/core/transformer/multi_latent_attention.py#L538-L548) registered up-projection replay on the core-attention output, allowing the parent's projection-output hook to run first.

**Correction:** Make the attention/TransformerLayer hook boundary enforce `input-layernorm restoration → MLA up-projection replay → core-attention replay → projection backward`. Account for both `attention_bda_and_cross_attention` and [`_forward_self_attention_output_with_bias`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/091d511c133395734cbffe805191959cfbd6430a/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L717-L720). The exact graph-boundary implementation needs verification against CUDA-graph/offload contracts; simply reversing all hooks or restoring the old up-projection placement is not a complete fix.

**Preservation:** Keep the current Q/K/V-before-core-attention ordering when both recomputation modules are selected. Retain ordinary MLA with Q-LoRA, up-projection-only recomputation, MHA/gated attention, and the packed/unpacked cases.

**Acceptance — proposed regression checks, not executed:** Use the new test's small BF16 MLA dimensions inside a full `TransformerLayer`, but set `q_lora_rank=None`; compare `["layernorm", "mla_up_proj"]` and `["layernorm", "mla_up_proj", "core_attn"]` against identical non-recomputed models. Backward must complete, the normalized input storage must be restored before up-projection replay reads it, and outputs plus input/parameter gradients must match. Retain the [existing test's](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/091d511c133395734cbffe805191959cfbd6430a/tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_core_attention_recompute.py#L92-L124) two-outstanding-graph, zero-storage-before-backward, restored-storage-after-backward, and gradient-parity assertions.

The strict review passed with no significant issues. Both findings from the previous review (5454498833, head `091d511c`) are fixed at `af19152e`, and nothing new qualifies.

This is a follow-up review, so the scope was:
- checking both findings from the previous review;
- checking the one production change made since then, the new viewless return boundary in MLA;
- checking how the PR fits with code merged from `main` since then, including the rewritten `CheckpointWithoutOutput`.

Findings: CRITICAL: 0, IMPORTANT: 0, SUGGESTION: 0.

**Fixed: input-layernorm output is now restored before the MLA up-projection is recomputed.**
- **Change.** [`MultiLatentAttention.forward`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/af19152ef2cf1137f96f41b3e1f00dc850f66850/megatron/core/transformer/multi_latent_attention.py#L650-L664) still registers the up-projection recompute hook and then the core-attention recompute hook on the `linear_proj` output. It now returns `make_viewless_tensor(output.view_as(output), ..., keep_graph=True)` instead of the output itself.
- **Why it works.**
  - `view_as` always produces a view, so `MakeViewlessTensor` always adds a pass-through autograd node. The returned tensor shares the output's storage and nothing is copied.
  - The enclosing layer registers its input-layernorm recompute hook on this returned tensor in both call paths: [`_forward_self_attention_output_with_bias`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/af19152ef2cf1137f96f41b3e1f00dc850f66850/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L722-L725) and [`attention_bda_and_cross_attention`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/af19152ef2cf1137f96f41b3e1f00dc850f66850/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L749-L754).
  - That hook therefore runs one node before the hooks on `output`. Backward order is now: input layernorm, then MLA up-projection, then core attention, then `linear_proj` backward.
  - The [rewritten checkpoint](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/af19152ef2cf1137f96f41b3e1f00dc850f66850/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/random.py#L970-L1026) points the restored layernorm output's storage at the recomputed data. The up-projection's saved input aliases that same storage, so with `q_lora_rank=None` it reads restored data.
- **What is preserved.** With Q-LoRA, with up-projection-only recompute, and with up-projection plus core attention, the up-projection is still recomputed before core attention.
- **Test.** The new [`test_layernorm_before_mla_recompute`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/af19152ef2cf1137f96f41b3e1f00dc850f66850/tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_core_attention_recompute.py#L127-L243) covers both layer call paths, packed and unpacked inputs, and core-attention recompute on and off, with two forward graphs alive at once.
  - It only identifies a checkpoint when the module already holds it as `input_layernorm_checkpoint`, `qkv_up_checkpoint` or `_core_attn_checkpoint` when `.checkpoint()` runs. All three are assigned before that call.
  - For each graph it checks the exact order of `norm`, `up` and `core` recompute events. It also checks that the layernorm output's storage is non-empty before the up-projection and core attention recompute, and that outputs and gradients match a non-recomputed model.

**Fixed: double-quoted test literals.** [L52](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/af19152ef2cf1137f96f41b3e1f00dc850f66850/tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_core_attention_recompute.py#L52) now uses `"selective"` and [L82](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/af19152ef2cf1137f96f41b3e1f00dc850f66850/tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_core_attention_recompute.py#L82) uses `device="cuda"`.

**Regression check of the new return boundary.** I found no regression:
- **Activation offloading.** When `attn_proj` offloading is on, the offload commit node was already downstream of the layer's hook in the previous review; the new node does nothing.
- **CUDA graphs.** The MLA output stays inside the captured region.
- **Inference.** Under `no_grad` the cost is one 1-element allocation per layer. On the fused TP-communication path the returned tensor shares storage with the original, and nothing checks its identity.
- **Other callers.** DSA, multi-token prediction, the HybridStack raw and shortcut paths, fine-grained callables, mHC, and residual-stream recompute are unaffected. `AbsorbedMLA` has its own `forward`.

# What does this PR do?

Make selective `core_attn` recomputation release the attention output retained by the output projection, reducing activation memory with fused attention.

In our fused-attention comparison, enabling ordinary `core_attn` checkpointing did not reduce peak activation memory. The output projection still saves the core-attention output for its weight gradient. This PR replaces ordinary checkpointing with `CheckpointWithoutOutput`: discard the attention output after projection and restore it before projection backward consumes it. The existing selective-recompute configuration remains the entry point.

Register recomputation on the projection output so that restoration precedes both projection backward and optional output-gate backward. When `mla_up_proj` recomputation is also enabled, register its hook first on the same tensor: restore Q/K/V, then recompute core attention.

Reject selective `core_attn` recomputation combined with `attn_proj` activation offloading during configuration validation, because both manage the projection-input storage. Remove the obsolete fused-attention recomputation warning and update the existing documentation to classify `core_attn` as output-discarding checkpointing.

## Issue tracking

Related to [#1886](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/1886), which reports no memory reduction with `core_attn` checkpointing and uses fused attention in its reproducer. This change improves memory savings by releasing the attention output retained for projection backward.

## Validation

### Added unit tests

- `tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_core_attention_recompute.py`: 32 parameterized GPU / Transformer Engine cases (4 attention variants × 2 sequence layouts × 2 dropout settings × 2 backends). Cover MHA, gated attention, MLA, and MLA with up-projection recomputation; packed/unpacked inputs; and FlashAttention/fused attention. Check storage discard/restoration, outputs, input/parameter gradients, and two outstanding forward graphs.
- `tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_transformer_config.py`: 24 added parameterized cases, comprising 12 conflict-rejection cases and 12 nonconflicting cases across `TransformerConfig` and `MLATransformerConfig`.

### End-to-end training

Separately from the committed unit tests, we ran five end-to-end DeepSeek-V2 Lite training controls.

Configuration: one node with 8 devices; 27 layers, hidden size 2048, 16 attention heads, sequence length 4096, BF16, FlashAttention, TP=1 / PP=4 / EP=2 / DP=2, microbatch size 1, global batch size 8, mock data, seed 42, and 20 training steps. All controls use the same execution environment and fusion settings. Initial parameter hashes match at every rank.

All five runs complete 20 forward/backward and optimizer steps, exit successfully, and record finite losses and gradient norms with no skipped steps.

#### Activation memory

Report the maximum of the per-rank `max_memory_allocated` measurements for training step 20.

| Recompute configuration | Step-20 max allocated memory (GiB) | Step-20 training loss |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Ordinary `core_attn` checkpoint | 54.107 | 8.733608 |
| Ordinary `core_attn`, independent repeat | 54.091 | 8.737156 |
| Discard-output `core_attn` | 53.663 | 8.736550 |
| Ordinary `core_attn` + `mla_up_proj` | 51.782 | 8.745314 |
| Discard-output `core_attn` + `mla_up_proj` | 51.338 | 8.740759 |

Switching core attention to discard-output reduces peak allocated memory by **0.444 GiB (454.6 MiB)**. With `mla_up_proj` recomputation already enabled, it saves a further **0.444 GiB (454.9 MiB)** relative to the matching ordinary-core-checkpoint control. Instrumentation also confirms that the core-attention output storage is released after projection.

#### Training numerical consistency

Compare matching iterations across all 20 steps. Gradient-norm differences below refer to the scalar norm logged by the trainer.

| Comparison | Maximum absolute loss difference | Maximum relative gradient-norm difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Independent repeat vs. ordinary `core_attn` baseline | 0.014456 | 1.937% |
| Discard-output vs. ordinary `core_attn` | 0.003868 | 0.584% |
| Discard-output vs. ordinary `core_attn`, both with `mla_up_proj` | 0.007325 | 1.118% |

For `core_attn` alone, both differences are smaller than those observed between independent baseline repeats. These measurements assess short-run training consistency over 20 steps with mock data.

**Restore input-layernorm output before MLA up-projection replay.**

**Failure:** Build a training `TransformerLayer` with the TE MLA submodules, `q_lora_rank=None`, and selective `recompute_modules=["layernorm", "mla_up_proj"]`; run forward and backward on a gradient-enabled input. Without Q-LoRA, [`_qkv_down_projection`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/091d511c133395734cbffe805191959cfbd6430a/megatron/core/transformer/multi_latent_attention.py#L727-L746) passes the normalized hidden states directly through as `q_compressed`. That tensor becomes a saved input of the up-projection checkpoint.

This change registers up-projection replay on the projection output **before** the enclosing layer registers its [input-layernorm restoration hook](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/091d511c133395734cbffe805191959cfbd6430a/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L743-L749) on the same tensor. Hooks execute in registration order, so up-projection replay reads the still-discarded, zero-byte normalized input. Backward must instead restore that input before recomputing `linear_q_proj`. The [base implementation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b67127774ca558442fb566a3df6a50862c04e4b8/megatron/core/transformer/multi_latent_attention.py#L538-L548) registered up-projection replay on the core-attention output, allowing the parent's projection-output hook to run first.

**Correction:** Make the attention/TransformerLayer hook boundary enforce `input-layernorm restoration → MLA up-projection replay → core-attention replay → projection backward`. Account for both `attention_bda_and_cross_attention` and [`_forward_self_attention_output_with_bias`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/091d511c133395734cbffe805191959cfbd6430a/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L717-L720). The exact graph-boundary implementation needs verification against CUDA-graph/offload contracts; simply reversing all hooks or restoring the old up-projection placement is not a complete fix.

**Preservation:** Keep the current Q/K/V-before-core-attention ordering when both recomputation modules are selected. Retain ordinary MLA with Q-LoRA, up-projection-only recomputation, MHA/gated attention, and the packed/unpacked cases.

**Acceptance — proposed regression checks, not executed:** Use the new test's small BF16 MLA dimensions inside a full `TransformerLayer`, but set `q_lora_rank=None`; compare `["layernorm", "mla_up_proj"]` and `["layernorm", "mla_up_proj", "core_attn"]` against identical non-recomputed models. This is a follow-up review, so the scope was:
- checking both findings from the previous review;

Findings: CRITICAL: 0, IMPORTANT: 0, SUGGESTION: 0.

**Fixed: input-layernorm output is now restored before the MLA up-projection is recomputed.**
- **Change.** [`MultiLatentAttention.forward`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/af19152ef2cf1137f96f41b3e1f00dc850f66850/megatron/core/transformer/multi_latent_attention.py#L650-L664) still registers the up-projection recompute hook and then the core-attention recompute hook on the `linear_proj` output. It now returns `make_viewless_tensor(output.view_as(output), ..., keep_graph=True)` instead of the output itself.
- **Why it works.**
  - `view_as` always produces a view, so `MakeViewlessTensor` always adds a pass-through autograd node. The returned tensor shares the output's storage and nothing is copied.
  - The enclosing layer registers its input-layernorm recompute hook on this returned tensor in both call paths: [`_forward_self_attention_output_with_bias`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/af19152ef2cf1137f96f41b3e1f00dc850f66850/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L722-L725) and [`attention_bda_and_cross_attention`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/af19152ef2cf1137f96f41b3e1f00dc850f66850/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L749-L754).
  - That hook therefore runs one node before the hooks on `output`. Backward order is now: input layernorm, then MLA up-projection, then core attention, then `linear_proj` backward.
  - The [rewritten checkpoint](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/af19152ef2cf1137f96f41b3e1f00dc850f66850/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/random.py#L970-L1026) points the restored layernorm output's storage at the recomputed data. The up-projection's saved input aliases that same storage, so with `q_lora_rank=None` it reads restored data.
- **What is preserved.** With Q-LoRA, with up-projection-only recompute, and with up-projection plus core attention, the up-projection is still recomputed before core attention.
- **Test.** The new [`test_layernorm_before_mla_recompute`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/af19152ef2cf1137f96f41b3e1f00dc850f66850/tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_core_attention_recompute.py#L127-L243) covers both layer call paths, packed and unpacked inputs, and core-attention recompute on and off, with two forward graphs alive at once.
  - It only identifies a checkpoint when the module already holds it as `input_layernorm_checkpoint`, `qkv_up_checkpoint` or `_core_attn_checkpoint` when `.checkpoint()` runs. All three are assigned before that call.
  - For each graph it checks the exact order of `norm`, `up` and `core` recompute events. It also checks that the layernorm output's storage is non-empty before the up-projection and core attention recompute, and that outputs and gradients match a non-recomputed model.

**Fixed: double-quoted test literals.** [L52](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/af19152ef2cf1137f96f41b3e1f00dc850f66850/tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_core_attention_recompute.py#L52) now uses `"selective"` and [L82](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/af19152ef2cf1137f96f41b3e1f00dc850f66850/tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_core_attention_recompute.py#L82) uses `device="cuda"`.

**Regression check of the new return boundary.** I found no regression:
- **Activation offloading.** When `attn_proj` offloading is on, the offload commit node was already downstream of the layer's hook in the previous review; the new node does nothing.
- **CUDA graphs.** The MLA output stays inside the captured region.
- **Inference.** Under `no_grad` the cost is one 1-element allocation per layer. On the fused TP-communication path the returned tensor shares storage with the original, and nothing checks its identity.
- **Other callers.** DSA, multi-token prediction, the HybridStack raw and shortcut paths, fine-grained callables, mHC, and residual-stream recompute are unaffected. `AbsorbedMLA` has its own `forward`.

- Unchanged since the previous review:
  - the new config check rejecting `core_attn` recompute combined with `attn_proj` offloading, and its tests;
  - the updated docstring and README.

**Overall risk: low.** The change is limited to where hooks are registered and when storage is released, and dependencies are now recomputed in the right order.
